The General Manager, Southern Railway, Headquarters, Park Town, Chennai - 600 003; 3. The Divisional Railway Manager, Southern Railway, Palakkad Division, Palakkad - 678 009; 4. Union of India, represented by Secretary, Railway Board, Rail Bhavan, New Delhi - 110 001; 5. The Secretary, Department of Personnel & Training, North Block, New Delhi - 110 001

facts_of_case: Sobhana V filed an application before the Central Administrative Tribunal, Ernakulam Bench, dated 16.12.2014 (O.A.No.180/01106/14). The railways filed a reply statement dated 30.06.2015. The case came up for admission on 29-07-2016.

legal_principles.principle: A divorced daughter of a deceased Railway servant is not eligible for family pension.
legal_principles.held: However, as the status of the applicant in that case as a divorcee has been declared only by the decree of the Family Court which was passed after the death of her father, we are of the view that her prayer for treating her as eligible for family pension cannot be granted.

legal_principles.principle: The purpose and intent of the orders are crucial in determining their applicability.
legal_principles.held: Instead of challenging Annexures A6 and A7 in O.A.No.1106 of 2014, the petitioner/applicant contended that, the purpose and intend of the said orders is not to grant family pension to those who were married and residing with their husband at the time of death of the Railway servant, which orders have no application in her case...

outcome.final_order: The court allowed the appeal and set aside the order of the Central Administrative Tribunal, Ernakulam Bench, dated 12-07-2016.

use_for_drafting: assisting with property disputes in joint families
